question: How do we view sleep in modern physiology?

options.C: A complete shutdown of brain activity

explanation: You might think the brain switches off at night, but sleep is actually a busy, organized state managed by specific brain networks. Great job keeping up with your physiology! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h1)

question: What happens to the body when someone goes without sleep for too long?
explanation: Missing sleep puts stress on your body and wears down your immune defenses. Remember to get some rest during exam prep week! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for keeping you awake and alert?
explanation: The reticular activating system acts like an internal alarm clock, sending steady wake-up signals to your brain. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h2)

question: What happens when the sleep-promoting centers quiet down the reticular activating system?
explanation: When those wake-up signals from the reticular activating system quiet down, your brain is finally able to drift off to sleep. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h2)

question: Which type of brain waves show up on an EEG when you are awake and fully focused?
explanation: Beta waves are fast and small, showing that your brain is actively working and alert—just like when you are studying your nursing notes! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h3)

question: Which brain wave pattern takes over during deep, restful slow-wave sleep?
explanation: Delta waves are slow and tall, showing up during deep sleep when your body gets its best physical rest. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h3)

question: During which stage of sleep do you experience vivid dreams and temporary muscle relaxation?
explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is when most dreaming happens. Your body temporarily relaxes your muscles so you don't act out your dreams! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h4)

question: About how long does one full sleep cycle (moving through NREM and REM stages) last?
explanation: Your brain cycles through different sleep stages roughly every hour and a half all night long. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h4)

question: Which structure acts as the body's master biological clock for daily rhythms?
explanation: Found in the hypothalamus, the suprachiasmatic nucleus uses light cues from your eyes to manage your 24-hour body clock. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why do night-shift nurses often find it hard to sleep during the day? Daytime light affects which hormone?
explanation: Daylight tells your biological clock to keep melatonin levels low, which is why sleeping during the day after a night shift can be so tough. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h5)

question: Which chemical builds up in your brain throughout the day to make you feel sleepy?
explanation: Adenosine piles up the longer you stay awake, creating sleep pressure until you finally rest and clear it out. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is the main job of the neurotransmitter GABA when you fall asleep?

options.A: Increasing body temperature and heart rate
options.B: Inhibiting wakefulness centers to allow rest

explanation: GABA is your brain's main calming chemical. It dials down the wake-up centers so you can finally relax and sleep. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h6)

question: Which part of the nervous system takes over during non-REM sleep to slow your heart rate and lower blood pressure?
explanation: The parasympathetic system is your 'rest and digest' mode. It slows things down so your body can conserve energy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h7)

question: Which hormone gets a major boost in release during deep, slow-wave sleep?
explanation: Deep sleep triggers a big release of growth hormone, which helps your body repair tissues and recover from the day's stress. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h7)

question: Which sleep disorder involves the upper airway repeatedly collapsing while a person sleeps?
explanation: In obstructive sleep apnea, throat muscles relax too much during sleep and temporarily block airflow, causing the person to briefly wake up to breathe. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h8)

question: A patient suddenly falls asleep during the day and feels weak when feeling strong emotions. What condition is this?
explanation: Narcolepsy causes sudden sleep attacks during the day. Strong emotions can sometimes trigger sudden muscle weakness called cataplexy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h8)
